importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is significant — an industrial PEB shed, a poultry farm shed, a terrace roofing shed, and a marriage hall shed are visually distinct structures. Buyers use the image to identify the correct product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Clear span, eave height, roofing material, and service model (supply-only vs turnkey) are primary shortlisting criteria for a capital construction purchase. Without these specs, a buyer cannot evaluate structural fit or project scope.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall — market is fragmented across regional fabricators and national players (EPACK, Kirby, Interarch); buyers search by spec, location, and price rather than brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: Capital construction project with post-sale dependency (erection, structural compliance, warranty) means buyers evaluate manufacturer status, IS compliance track record, and past project portfolio before committing. Seller credibility is a meaningful shortlisting signal.

Per-sq-ft rate is a budget entry point that Indian buyers compare across sellers, but price changes substantially with span, height, insulation type, and service model — making it a post-spec-shortlisting signal rather than a primary filter. Final price is always project-quoted and negotiated.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Sub-segments quote differently — supply-only steel components may be quoted per kg, and large turnkey contracts as a lump-sum project cost. Per sq ft is the dominant and most buyer-comparable unit and must be shown to prevent price misreading across these quoting conventions.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per kg vs per project is a real market ambiguity confirmed across multiple Indian PEB manufacturer sources. Price cannot be meaningfully compared without knowing the unit basis.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Span is the primary structural dimension — non-interchangeable across project requirements (a buyer needing 80 ft clear span cannot use a 30 ft structure) and the largest single driver of steel tonnage and therefore price.

PEB vs Conventional vs Trussless defines the entire construction system — non-interchangeable across engineering approach, supplier capability, and price point, making it the fundamental product class separator.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Insulation type (PUF panel, rock wool, glass wool, or none) is a primary thermal performance and cost driver — PUF sandwich panels vs uninsulated GI sheet represent fundamentally different product configurations that buyers specify upfront, not an accessory add-on.

Supply-only vs supply-and-erect vs full turnkey (design + fabrication + erection) defines the entire scope of the seller's offering — a supply-only fabricator and a turnkey contractor are different seller types that buyers must distinguish before engaging.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Shed type routes the RFQ to the correct seller category — a PEB industrial shed supplier cannot serve a poultry shed buyer, making this the primary seller-routing signal.
Project area defines scale and determines whether a seller's capacity and minimum order threshold match the buyer's requirement, enabling sellers to self-select before responding.

missing_important_specs.why_important: A supply-only fabricator cannot serve a buyer requiring turnkey erection — sellers need this to determine whether they can fulfil the requirement before responding to the RFQ.

Span width is the primary structural dimension — sellers cannot assess feasibility or provide an accurate quote without knowing the required clear span, as it determines steel tonnage and engineering complexity.
